ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Amara Okafor, MD
Department: Pulmonary & Critical Care
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Progressive dyspnea on exertion and dry cough over the past 6 months.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
She presents to the clinic with a 6-month history of progressive dyspnea on exertion and a dry cough. She denies any chest pain, orthopnea, or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. She has not noticed any changes in her skin or joint symptoms recently.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Systemic sclerosis (scleroderma), limited cutaneous subtype, diagnosed 5 years prior
- Raynaud phenomenon
- Gastroesophageal reflux disease

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Appendectomy (age 15)
- Cesarean section (age 28)

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Mother: Rheumatoid arthritis
- Father: Hypertension
- Sister: Hashimoto thyroiditis

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Social, 1-2 drinks per month. Occupation: Administrative assistant.

VITAL SIGNS:
On physical examination, her blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg, heart rate is 88 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation is 96% on room air.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Auscultation of the lungs reveals no crackles, wheezes, or rhonchi. Cardiac examination shows a loud P2 component of the second heart sound. There is no peripheral edema.

LABORATORY DATA:
Laboratory tests reveal normal complete blood count and renal function.

IMAGING:
An echocardiogram demonstrates normal left ventricular size and function, but there is evidence of right ventricular hypertrophy and an estimated right ventricular systolic pressure of 55 mmHg.

OTHER STUDIES:
Pulmonary function tests show a normal FEV1 and FEV1/FVC ratio with a reduced diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO).

attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2021-01-15
Provider: Dr. Amara Okafor, MD
Department: Pulmonary & Critical Care
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Gradually worsening shortness of breath and fatigue over the past year, now with reduced exercise tolerance.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient with limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis returns to Pulmonary & Critical Care one year following her initial evaluation. She presents with gradually worsening shortness of breath and fatigue over the past year, noting she gets winded climbing stairs and sometimes feels lightheaded while walking quickly.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Pulmonary arterial hypertension associated with systemic sclerosis (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Systemic sclerosis (scleroderma), limited cutaneous subtype, diagnosed 5 years prior
- Raynaud phenomenon
- Gastroesophageal reflux disease

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Appendectomy (age 15)
- Cesarean section (age 28)

MEDICATIONS:
She takes no daily medications.

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Mother: Rheumatoid arthritis
- Father: Hypertension
- Sister: Hashimoto thyroiditis

SOCIAL HISTORY:
She has no history of smoking

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Physical examination reveals clear lungs, elevated jugular venous pressure, and a loud P2 heart sound.

IMAGING:
Chest x-ray shows enlarged central pulmonary arteries with clear lung fields.

OTHER STUDIES:
Right heart catheterization confirms elevated pulmonary arterial pressures with normal pulmonary capillary wedge pressure.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN:
She is diagnosed with idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension

Started on bosentan therapy.
